findings.problem: This snapshot calls her 'Alice Turner' and 'Alice', but her first name is not given until [4:200]. Until then the text, and her own card name, use only 'Miss Turner'. This is not a plot spoiler, but it is inconsistent with her own card, which deliberately holds the name back.
findings.evidence: [4:113] "goading him on to propose to Miss Turner"; first 'Alice' at [4:200] "I should wish to spare Alice the shock"
findings.fix: BODY from [4:113]: "The eighteen-year-old son of Charles McCarthy, held for trial for his father’s murder; Miss Turner and Holmes believe him innocent. Holmes learns that he loves Miss Turner but, about two years ago, secretly married a Bristol barmaid. That is why he resisted his father’s pressure to propose, and why he spent the days before the killing in Bristol. The barmaid has now broken with him, revealing she already had a husband."

findings.problem: The thread calls his daughter 'Alice', a name the story withholds until [4:200]. Her own card and thread name her only as 'Miss Turner'.
findings.evidence: [4:21] "Miss Turner, the daughter of the neighbouring landowner"
findings.fix: "The wealthy landowner of Boscombe Valley, who made his fortune in Australia. He is Charles McCarthy’s landlord and old friend from the colonies, and the father of Miss Turner."

findings.problem: 'his daughter never learned the truth' states as a settled fact something Watson gives only as a prospect at the time of writing.
findings.evidence: [4:214] "there is every prospect that the son and daughter may come to live happily together in ignorance of the black cloud which rests upon their past"
findings.fix: Replace the last sentence with: "Holmes kept the confession unused, and Turner lived seven months more before he died. Watson writes that his daughter and young McCarthy may yet live happily together, unaware of the past."

findings.problem: All of the content in the [4:200] snapshot is known by [4:86]: she has known James since childhood, McCarthy wanted the marriage and her father opposed it. Meanwhile, from [4:76] to [4:199], readers who tap 'Miss Turner' see only the thin [4:21] card. Only the first name 'Alice' is new at [4:200].
findings.evidence: [4:76] "We have known each other since we were little children"; [4:84] "Mr. McCarthy was very anxious that there should be a marriage between us"; [4:86] "No, he was averse to it also."
findings.fix: Add a snapshot gated at [4:86], NAME "Miss Turner", BODY: "John Turner’s only daughter, who has known James McCarthy since childhood and is sure he is innocent. She brought in Lestrade and Holmes to clear him. She tells Holmes that Charles McCarthy wanted her to marry James, a match both James and her father opposed." Keep the [4:200] snapshot only for the name change to "Alice Turner".

findings.problem: Turner's illness ([4:88]-[4:90], [4:117]-[4:119]) and his rent-free generosity to McCarthy ([4:119]) are facts Holmes reasons from at [4:122], but his card stays on the [4:16] text until [4:192]. These facts are safe to show: they appear in the text and point to no one.
findings.evidence: [4:119] "About sixty; but his constitution has been shattered by his life abroad ... he gave him Hatherley Farm rent free."
findings.fix: Add a snapshot gated at [4:119]: "The largest landowner in Boscombe Valley, about sixty, who made his fortune in the Victorian goldfields. Long in poor health, he has taken to his bed since McCarthy’s death. Lestrade says he was McCarthy’s great benefactor and let him have Hatherley Farm rent free."

findings.problem: 'he is said to be cold and forbidding in manner' comes from James's statement at [4:37], 21 paragraphs after the gate. This is minor characterisation, but it runs ahead of the text.
findings.evidence: [4:37] "He was not a popular man, being somewhat cold and forbidding in his manners"
findings.fix: BODY from [4:16]: "A former Australian colonist who rents Hatherley Farm from his old acquaintance John Turner. A widower with one son, James." Optionally carry 'cold and forbidding in manner, as his son describes him' into a snapshot gated at [4:37].

findings.problem: 'Moran' at [4:135] is the lodge-keeper, Patience Moran's father, who carries Holmes's note to Turner ([4:188]). It is unbound, and the lodge-keeper card never gives his surname.
findings.evidence: [4:135] "this grey house on the right must be the lodge. I think that I will go in and have a word with Moran, and perhaps write a little note."
findings.fix: Bind "Moran" at [4:135] (original-en and modern-en) to boscombe-lodge-keeper. Change the card's BODY to: "Moran, keeper of the lodge on John Turner’s Boscombe Valley estate and father of Patience Moran. His lodge was the nearest house to the pool."

findings.problem: The cultural reference 'Baxter's words' is unbound, although Petrarch and Meredith in the same story have cards. Holmes gives the saying to Baxter, usually understood as the Puritan Richard Baxter, but it is more commonly credited to John Bradford, so the card needs to state that uncertainty.
findings.evidence: [4:213] "I never hear of such a case as this that I do not think of Baxter’s words, and say, ‘There, but for the grace of God, goes Sherlock Holmes.’"
findings.fix: Add reference/cultural-figure card bound at [4:213] 'Baxter' (both editions): NAME "Baxter" | SUBTITLE "English Puritan writer" | BODY "Usually taken to be Richard Baxter (1615–1691), the English Puritan minister and writer. Holmes credits him with the saying ‘There, but for the grace of God, goes …’, which tradition more often attributes to the Protestant martyr John Bradford."
